handbookNote: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017, with a Massachusetts-specific front matter/Preface revised March 2025), published by the Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- fetched directly from https://www.mass.gov/doc/cdl-manual-march-2025-version/download on 2026-08-22 (5.46MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/ma_cdl_research/ma_cdl_manual_full.txt, 10,978 lines). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics, confirmed directly from the official Massachusetts-specific Preface of this manual (Commercial Driver's License Tests / Knowledge Tests list): the General Knowledge Test is taken by all applicants (1 hour, 50 questions); the Passenger Transport Test is taken by all bus driver applicants (20 minutes, 20 questions); the Air Brakes Test is required for vehicles with air brakes (25 minutes, 25 questions); the Combination Vehicles Test is required to drive combination vehicles (20 minutes, 20 questions); the Hazardous Materials Test is required to haul hazardous material or waste (30 minutes, 30 questions); the Tanker Test is required to haul liquids in bulk (20 minutes, 20 questions); the Doubles/Triples Test is required to pull double or triple trailers (20 minutes, 20 questions); and the School Bus Test is required to transport pre-primary/primary/secondary students in a full-sized school bus -- notably, unlike every other test in this same list, the Preface does NOT disclose an item count or time limit for the School Bus Test, so that figure is explicitly left unconfirmed in this question bank rather than guessed or borrowed from another state (consistent with this project's no-default-values discipline; AL, AR, KS, and IN CDL tracks had similar hedged item counts). For every test, 80 percent of questions must be answered correctly to pass, which is also the federally standardized minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a). Massachusetts's three CDL vehicle classes are A (combination vehicles, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), B (single vehicle or combination, GVWR 26,001+ lbs, towed unit 10,000 lbs GVWR or less), and C (vehicle not meeting Class A/B definitions but designed to carry 16+ passengers including the driver, or placarded for hazardous materials); available endorsements are Double/Triple Trailers, Tank Vehicles, Tank Vehicles with HAZMAT, HAZMAT, Passenger Transport Vehicles, and School Bus. Massachusetts-specific administrative detail confirmed directly from the manual's Preface and layered into the licensing bucket: CLPs are valid 180 days and may be renewed once for an additional 180 days; CDL applicants must be 18 for intrastate operation (with a mandatory K restriction under age 21) and 21 for interstate/unrestricted operation; there is a mandatory 14-day wait between CLP issuance and the road-test appointment; the CDL Skills Test has three parts (pre-trip inspection, off-street skills test, on-road test); operating a full-sized school bus requires both a Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsement plus a School Bus Driver Certificate from the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities, which in turn requires 3 continuous years of driving experience, a CORI check, a SORI check, a DOT physical, and Basic First Aid Training; the Hazardous Materials endorsement requires a TSA fingerprint-based background check (via IBT/universalenroll.dhs.gov) and is never transferable from another state or issuable on a CLP; DOT medical certificates are valid for a maximum of two years; the four CDL self-certification categories are Non-Excepted Interstate (NI), Excepted Interstate (EI), Non-Excepted Intrastate (NA), and Excepted Intrastate (EA), with NI/NA drivers re-certifying at least every two years and EI/EA drivers every five years; Massachusetts-based disqualifications under M.G.L. c.90F sec.9 impose a minimum 1-year CDL loss (3 years if the vehicle was hazmat-placarded) for a first alcohol/drug/refusal/felony-use offense, and a lifetime loss for a second such offense; the federal disqualification tables at 49 CFR 383.51 (Tables 1-4, reproduced in the Preface) separately govern major-offense, serious-traffic-violation, railroad-crossing, and out-of-service-order penalties; and a Lifetime Disqualification Waiver Program (effective for applications beginning July 18, 2025 per 540 CMR 2.06(9)(c)(5)) allows eligible lifetime-disqualified drivers to apply for reinstatement after serving at least 10 years. Content-depth rationale: Massachusetts uses the same AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' base manual as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project, organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into three buckets for volume: 02_driving_safely_a covering vehicle inspection/basic control/shifting/seeing/communicating/speed/space management through subsection 2.7, 02b_seeing_hazards_distraction covering the seeing-hazards and distracted-driving subsections 2.8-2.9 including the federal hand-held-phone and texting disqualification rules, and 03_driving_safely_b covering night/extreme-condition driving, railroad crossings, mountain driving, emergency maneuvers, skid control, accident/fire procedures, and alcohol/drugs), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets), Section 10 School Buses (supplemented by the Preface's Massachusetts-specific School Bus Requirements/Driver Eligibility material), Section 11 Vehicle Inspection (this manual's Section 11 is specifically the CDL skills-test walkaround/air-brake-check checklist rather than a general inspection-philosophy narrative, and was questioned as such), Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving (12 and 13 combined into one bucket). Some sections (Cargo, Doubles/Triples, Tank Vehicles) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; conversely Sections 2, 9, 10, 11, and the Passenger section proved unusually dense with distinct testable facts/numbers and yielded above-typical counts. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Massachusetts manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers. One drafting agent flagged that the source PDF's two-column body layout can misorder text when read too literally line-by-line; this was checked via targeted spot-verification of numeric claims (e.g., the 119-gallon/1,000-gallon tank endorsement thresholds, the 55 psi low-air-warning threshold, the 3-year/CORI/SORI school bus eligibility requirements) directly against the extracted source text before this track was finalized, and all spot-checked facts matched the source exactly.
